title: Joke Goods
text: “The Mirror Vassal Weapon had an attack like that. If it keeps that thing deployed at all times, covering its entire body… there's no way to land a hit through ordinary means. And on top of that, the enemy gets to attack us while shifting its own existence to some other dimension? That’s just cruel.”
A cheat, an exploit—that’s what it amounts to, Father continued.
“If you use something inscribed with the characters I draw, you can cancel out that shift. That way, you’ll be able to properly cut right through them.”
“I see. Well, even if we managed that, whether it’d actually be enough to finish that thing off is another matter.”
“Yeah, probably. From what I heard, it was quite the opponent, so this alone would likely be rough.”
So even breaking through the barrier the Crimson Swine itself deployed wouldn’t be enough to finish it off on its own. Talk about a troublesome enemy, I say.

“By the way, if you apply this magical script, you can also keep your own clothes from catching fire when you unleash some big move. Just shift the space around the clothes alone, and they won’t tear, get dirty, or get wet. Oh, and something this minor won’t get flagged as cheating under this world’s laws.”
“Sounds like it’d be good for the Filolials’ clothes, Motoyasu.”
“Indeed it would! Hou-kun, teach me, I say!”
“Ehh! No way! I don’t really feel like teaching you!”
Hou-kun could be quite cold sometimes, I say.
“Setting up the canceling script isn’t all that hard, but… this world probably doesn’t even need it, does it?”
“…Yeah, probably not.”
Father agreed with Ark’s words. Big Sister nodded quietly as well. Since this world had become peaceful, such technology was simply excessive, I say.
“So it’s the kind of technology that disregards its own proper domain. The sort that the Holy Weapons, the Seven Star Weapons, and the Vassal Weapons would need to keep watch over.”
“I suppose that’s about right.”
And so, in that sort of way, Doctor was learning harmless alchemy techniques from Ark and the others.
Some time had passed since Hou-kun and the others came to the village, I say.
“Hmm… I can’t tell the difference between big bro’s cooking and Ark-san’s cooking anymore.”
Keel muttered this while eating the food served at dinner, I say.
“Well, that’s because I’ve been cooking together with Naofumi-kun.”
“There’s a lot of collaborative dishes too, since he matches my rhythm, it makes things easy.”
After cooking together so many times, Father and the others had apparently gotten the hang of each other’s pace, and now they seemed to cook in perfect sync, I say.
“Nom nom! Naofumi-kun and Kitty’s cooking is so yummy-fu!”
Somehow, Hou-kun was slurping his food with his beak. A steady slurp-slurp rang out, and he seemed to be eating quite happily, I say.
“More importantly, would you quit slurping your food as a bit sometimes.”
“I think maintaining at least a minimum of decency matters, even when you’re doing it as a joke.”
“I don’t know what kind of comedian you’re trying to be, but you should stop eating in a way that makes everyone around you uncomfortable.”
Hou-kun received sub-zero glares from both Father and Ark, but he looked utterly unbothered, as if the wind were simply passing him by.
“It’s delicious, but man, I miss my wife’s cooking.”
Hou-kun longed for the cooking of his wife, who—according to the story—had run away from him, I say.
“Your wife’s seasoning, huh.”
“What kind of taste was it?”
“Hmm, it changed depending on the occasion… but there was a pattern to it. The important thing was the fire, so—”
“Hold on! You don’t need to try recreating it! It feels like my precious memories are about to get overwritten, so just stop already!”

As if pleading with them to quit, Hou-kun cautioned Father and Ark. Indeed, Father was extremely skilled at recreating dishes—he could easily reproduce the taste of any restaurant. Ark seemed to have skills rivaling Father’s as well, so if the two of them put their minds to it, I was certain they could surely recreate the seasoning of Hou-kun’s wife that he longed for, I say.

“Honestly, that bird gets annoying sometimes, so maybe we should study his preferred seasoning until he can’t think about anything but food, or just threaten to withhold his favorite meal whenever he says something out of line.”
“Sounds good.”
“Naofumi-sama, I won’t let you say you’ve forgotten that you experimented on Keel-kun behind my back.”

At this, Big Sister spoke up, driving the point home to Father and Ark, who were scheming something wicked, I say. Apparently, because Father’s cooking was so delicious, he had once used Keel as a test subject to see just how far he could push feeding her favorite food. The goal seemed to be finding the balance where Keel wouldn’t overeat but would still feel satisfied, all to boost her motivation even further. Keel had been chosen both for her own personality and as a reward for the motivation and profits she brought in through her popularity, which rivaled even Filo-tan’s. On top of that, it apparently doubled as an experiment to test whether it was even possible, based on information that some reincarnators had been known to brainwash people through cooking…

For the first few days, nothing seemed particularly off about Keel, but before long her behavior gradually began to change. She threw herself into work with unusual intensity, and whenever mealtime rolled around, she would head toward Father with bloodshot eyes, I say. It was right around this point that Big Sister caught on, scolded Father, and the experiment was called off.
“The food big bro made just for me was super delicious, though…”
“Do you have any idea how hard it was to calm Keel-kun down when she wouldn’t stop complaining to me every time the seasoning changed!”
“Well, Raphtalia’s given us a no-go. Still, if the bird gets to be too much of a pain, I’ll keep the research in mind as an option.”
“That’s harsh. Oh, right. Motoyasu-kun~”
“What is it, I say?”
Hou-kun had called out to me, so I went over.
“What? Just because Motoyasu says something doesn’t mean your messy-eating punishment plan is scrapped.”

“Heh, if you think I’d learn my lesson that easily, you’re sorely mistaken. Let’s leave that topic there for now, Motoyasu-kun. You’ve been treating me like some kind of Filolial lately, so I prepared a little something as thanks.”
Hou-kun spread his wings and, using his beak, pulled something out from within them, setting it down in front of me. At first glance, it looked like a plate depicting a Filolial-sama’s backside.
“You probably think it’s just a plain plate and have no idea what it actually is, so let me explain. This is something you hang on the wall, and you hook the bottle cap right here to pop it open.”
With that, Hou-kun pointed to the little hole in the Filolial-sama’s backside with the tip of his wing.
“Whoa… to think you’d go and make such an elaborate joke item just to mess with someone…”
“Your sense of humor’s on par with some scatological old man’s. Is it worse that you made and gave this with clear malicious intent? No… wait, maybe having obvious malice actually makes it better?”
Father and the others seemed rather taken aback.
“Thank you very much, I say!”

Since Hou-kun had made and given me a piece of merchandise modeled after a Filolial-sama, I intended to treasure it no matter what it actually was! Any gift depicting a Filolial-sama was a precious treasure to me. That’s right—Filolial-sama, who took a liking to anything that shone, would sometimes bestow precious treasures upon me as gifts. And since this one came from someone who went around defeating things like the Crimson Swine itself, I would treasure it for the rest of my life, I say.
“No, wait, listen? This thing is meant to be used this way, and you’re supposed to react with either disgust or fury.”
“Thank you so much for making this for me, I say!”
“Wow… the sarcasm completely missed its mark. Watching that bird react like that is honestly hilarious.”
“Once Motoyasu’s designated you an honorary Filolial, nothing you do has any effect, huh… I knew it, but I have to admire just how thorough he is about it.”

At this point, Older Sister, undeterred as ever, came over to Father and the others carrying a bottle of liquor. Lately, rather than simply looking cheerful every day, she wore more of a relieved expression, as though she were savoring the peace with all her heart.
“Naofumi-chan and everyone~ let’s drink together again today~!”
“You get plastered every single day, and yet you never learn, huh.”
“Truly.”
“Older Sister! Hou-kun made me a wall-mounted bottle opener shaped like a Filolial-sama, I say!”
“Oh my? Is that so?”
Older Sister took her bottle and used the gift Hou-kun had given me—now mounted on the wall—to pop the cap open. It was right before that moment—
“Is the Dark Saint Hero here—”
Black Thunder, searching for Ren, entered the dining hall from right behind Older Sister. Just at that perfect moment, Older Sister had popped the cork with a satisfying pok.
